items.q: All of the following define glomerular hematuria in the flowchart EXCEPT:
items.exp: Glomerular hematuria: ≥ 40% dysmorphic RBCs / ≥ 5% acanthocytes / single RBC cast + proteinuria. (Book p742)

items.q: Fill up: Glomerular hematuria criteria include ≥ 40 % dysmorphic RBCs or ≥ ______ % acanthocytes or a single RBC cast with proteinuria.
items.exp: ≥ 40% dysmorphic RBCs / ≥ 5% acanthocytes / single RBC cast + proteinuria. (Book p742)

items.q: Once glomerular hematuria is established, the next step in the flowchart is biopsy, which typically reveals:
The mechanism written for hematuria in IgA nephropathy is:
opts: Mesangial proliferation + matrix expansion → capillary rupture
items.exp: Mesangial proliferation + matrix expansion → capillary rupture. (Book p742)

items.q: When the settled RBCs point to a urological cause, the appropriate next step is:
opts: Radiological investigation with USG abdomen and CT
Cystoscopy with biopsy as first step
items.exp: Urological cause → radiological Ix (USG abdomen, CT). (Book p742)

items.q: A still high-colored supernatant is left undisturbed for how long before judging the colour?
items.exp: Sample undisturbed for 3-6 hours, then observe whether the colour fades or persists. (Book p742)

items.q: A crushed-limb injury patient passes dark urine; the supernatant colour fades over a few hours. The pigment and its source are:
items.exp: Colour fades → myoglobin (short t½): rhabdomyolysis. (Book p742)

items.q: Which statement about the standing-supernatant test is TRUE?
opts: A persistent colour implies hemoglobin with a long half-life from hemolysis
A persistent colour implies myoglobin from rhabdomyolysis
A fading colour implies hemoglobin from hemolysis
The test distinguishes porphyria from beetroot intake
items.exp: Persistent colour → hemoglobin (long t½): hemolysis; fading → myoglobin (short t½). (Book p742)
